message: Complete setup for visual review: retain the current geometry, illustrative aluminum and rear restraint; replace the 100 N load with 150 N downward on face 9. Both bores remain free. Apply and confirm the setup before solving; previous results do not represent this load.

simulation_proposal.notes: Fully fix the entire rear X=0 face (1) in XYZ. Apply a TOTAL force [0,0,-150] N uniformly over the selected X=80 end face (9), replacing the previous force. Global X follows base length, Y spans width, and Z points upward. Bore surfaces 6 and 10 remain unrestrained and unloaded. This complete setup retains the existing geometry. Preview, apply and confirm before a new solve.
assumptions: Synthetic demonstration with explicitly adopted illustrative, uncertified material properties.
Homogeneous isotropic small-strain linear-elastic static response under steady room-temperature loading.
Rear support is an ideal full XYZ restraint.
No self-weight, contact, bolts or preload.
No acceptance threshold is specified; this proposal provides no physical approval.
The current 7 mm mesh is an initial mesh; sharp-corner and fixture-edge stresses require mesh-convergence assessment.

assumptions: The image is synthetic; all dimensions are supplied demonstration specifications in mm.
90° bracket: base occupies X=0–80, Y=0–40, Z=0–8; upright occupies X=0–8, Y=0–40, Z=0–60. Height is overall.
Both bores are plain Ø8 mm through-holes: base center X=57.6, Y=20, axis Z; upright center Y=20, Z=43.2, axis X.
No hidden features or fillets; the legs form one connected solid.
7 mm is the initial mesh size. Sharp internal-corner and fixture-edge stresses may be mesh-dependent; assess mesh convergence.
Material properties are illustrative, not certified. Analysis assumes homogeneous isotropic small-strain linear elasticity and a static load.
